lines.text: For four thousand years, the sculptors of ancient India carved the divine into bronze and stone.
At Mohenjo-daro, a bronze dancing girl stands in graceful defiance, adorned in twenty-two bangles.
At Sarnath, Emperor Ashoka crowns polished sandstone pillars with four lions and the turning wheel of law.
In the Gupta classical age, stone dissolves into meditation, radiating sublime peace and serenity.
Inside the rock-cut caves of Elephanta, three colossal faces of Shiva gaze across eternity.
Under the Cholas, Nataraja leaps into the ring of fire, dancing the cosmos into creation and release.
From sacred terracotta to immortal bronze, ancient India carved the eternal spirit into form.
